title.en: Trump launches fresh attack on Merz after threatening US troop reduction in Germany – Europe live

summary.en: US President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Angela Merkel on social media regarding Ukraine, immigration, and Iran, and threatened to reduce US troops in Germany.

reflection.en: International relations often involve complex disagreements, yet the pursuit of peace remains a vital aspiration. Even amidst political tensions and public criticisms, striving for peaceful coexistence and respectful dialogue is a shared responsibility.
reflection.zh: 国际关系常涉及复杂分歧，但追求和平仍是至关重要的愿望。即使在政治紧张和公开批评中，努力实现和平共处和相互尊重的对话，仍是共同的责任。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Farage did not need to declare £5m donation as it was ‘private’, claims Braverman – UK politics live
title.zh: 布雷弗曼声称法拉奇无需申报500万英镑捐款，因其属“私人”性质——英国政治直播

summary.en: Former Home Secretary Suella Braverman defended Reform UK leader Nigel Farage after reports that he did not declare a £5 million donation, claiming it was a “private” gift. This comes amidst a political debate where Farage has presented himself as “down to earth.”
summary.zh: 前内政大臣苏拉·布雷弗曼为英国改革党领袖奈杰尔·法拉奇辩护，此前有报道称他未申报一笔500万英镑的捐款，布雷弗曼称其为“私人”馈赠。此事发生之际，法拉奇在政治辩论中一直将自己塑造成“脚踏实地”的形象。

body.en: Former Tory home secretary turned Reform UK education spokesperson defends party leader over undeclared gift On BBC Radio Merseyside the presenter, Tony Snell , put it to Kemi Badenoch that Merseyside was a lost cause for the Tories. He said that Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, had been on the programme yesterday. He said that Farage argued that Scousers were down to earth and the Tories they were seen as “aloof and remote”. Badenoch said no one had ever described her as aloof and remote. When it was put to her that Farage was talking about the party, she said the Tories were the party of working people. Labour were only interested in welfare, she claimed. Nigel Farage can say as much as he wants that he’s the one who’s down to earth. Someone just gave him a £5m gift to the other day. I don’t know what’s down to earth about that. Who gets £5m is a gift. If I got £50,000 as a gift, I think people would raise their eyebrows. That’s a hundred times that. And he forgot to register it. He forgot that he’d been given £5m. I don’t think that’s down to earth. So I’m not going to be taking any lessons from Nigel Farage. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The news of an undeclared £5 million gift raises questions about transparency and integrity in public life, especially when a leader's image is built on being “down to earth.” This situation reminds us that true character is revealed not just in grand statements, but in consistent faithfulness, whether in small matters or significant ones.
reflection.zh: 一笔未申报的500万英镑捐款的消息，引发了人们对公共生活中透明度和诚信的质疑，尤其当一位领袖的形象是建立在“脚踏实地”之上时。这种情况提醒我们，真正的品格不仅体现在宏大的言辞中，更体现在无论是小事还是大事上始终如一的忠实。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

reflection.en: The UAE's decision to leave OPEC to pursue its own oil production goals highlights the tension between individual gain and collective stability. This move, while perhaps economically advantageous for one party, creates uncertainty and weakens a long-standing partnership. Proverbs 15:17 reminds us that the value of harmonious relationships often outweighs...

body.en: Human rights commissioner says alleged jailing highlights the ‘growing risks of transnational repression’ in Australia Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s human rights commissioner has said the Chinese student who was allegedly jailed for six years by Chinese authorities for joining protests in Sydney underscores the “very real and growing risks of transnational repression affecting people in Australia – including international students”. Commissioner Lorraine Finlay told Guardian Australia that while she could not comment on the circumstances of individual cases “no one should fear punishment abroad for exercising their lawful rights to free expression and peaceful protest here”.
